added_claim_errors: Says claiming at 62 is 60 months early and a flat 30% cut, then says entitlement starts April 2027 (59 months, 29.58%). Internally inconsistent, though the key accepts the 30% / $1,680 approximation.
Adds the 3.6% 2027 COLA as certain to reach $1,740 and $2,486. The key lists this as a side-claim trap, and $1,740 is not the key's roughly $1,690.

Says the earnings test 'takes most of those checks away' and calls it 'the worst of both'. About 4 of 9 checks in 2027 and about 3.6 of 12 in later years are withheld, and withheld months are partly recovered at FRA, so this overstates it.

Says for married filing jointly the federal tax line drops 'possibly to near zero'. My own rough recomputation (MFJ base amounts, standard deduction, about $14,660 net benefits) gives roughly $1,300 a year, so 'near zero' is unverified and probably too low.

Budget table smooths the earnings-test withholding at -$518 a month over 12 months and treats the full $1,740 as monthly income. It is labelled an annualized run-rate and later qualified, but it is not the 2027 cash-flow shape (little or no SS until about September).
Federal income tax of about $320 a month is an estimate with no stated brackets. My rough check (single, 2026 brackets) gives about $323, so it is plausible but not shown.
Cites SSA, POMS RS 00615.015 and Form SSA-521 links. I judged these from my own knowledge and did not open them. The SSA-521 withdrawal within 12 months with full repayment is correct.
Says 60 months early gives 'exactly 168/240' (70%), then says entitlement starts April 2027 (59 months, 29.58%). Inconsistent. It never gives the $1,680 figure the key accepts, only $1,740.
Adds the 3.6% 2027 COLA as certain to reach $2,486 and $1,740. The key lists this as a side-claim trap.

Says 'eight checks in calendar 2027' with 'roughly three and a half' swallowed and about $7,700 received. The $7,700 is 8 x $1,740 minus $6,220, which ignores whole-check withholding. About 4 checks are withheld, leaving about 4 checks (about $6,960, or about $6,760 without COLA). The 'not $14,660' comparison is also off, because 8 checks gross only $13,920.
Says 'Every dollar between $25,560 and $38,000 buys you 50 cents of benefit'. This is garbled: each dollar earned over the limit costs 50 cents of benefit.

Table is headed 'Monthly, 2027' and shows $1,222 of SS received every month. That is not the 2027 pattern (April start, whole checks withheld, little SS until about September). The later 'lumpy' note partly corrects it. It also subtracts FICA after calling it 'already deducted from wages', which is confusing.
Says you 'lose that $6,220 every year until March 2032'. The limit changes each year and withheld months are partly credited back at FRA, so the fixed figure is unverifiable.

Federal tax of $323 a month uses 2026 brackets (standard deduction $16,100; 10% to $12,400; 12% to $50,400). The arithmetic checks out (about $3,875 a year) and the answer flags it as an estimate. Applying the 2026 brackets to 2027 is an approximation.
Says waiting to 67 pays 'about 40% more'. $2,486 / $1,740 is about 43%, so this is acceptable as rounded.

reasons: Both answers catch both false premises at the start. Both get the April 2027 start, the $25,560 limit, the $12,440 excess and the $6,220 withholding. Both state the 85% taxable point and the recalculation at FRA. Both add the 3.6% COLA as certain (a key trap), and both say '60 months' while also placing entitlement in April (59 months). A is slightly better on the part the key stresses most, the 2027 cash flow. It labels its table an annualized run-rate and states that 2027 will be lumpy, with about four deposits and about $7,000, which matches the key's four withheld months and September start. B labels its smoothed table 'Monthly, 2027' and gives an off-target $7,700 with a garbled '50 cents of benefit' line. A shows the $1,680 / 30% figure the key accepts, where B shows only $1,740. B has useful extras (the comparison to her expected $5,567 and a health-insurance warning), but A has some overclaiming ('worst of both', 'most checks'). Neither gives a month-by-month budget, mentions the monthly rule, or points her to my Social Security or SSA's calculators.
